Ties the key at 14 words; the twin with the key is broken.

Breaks longest words, window overlap, passage overlap and the only-two-part tell; the measure shows none now picks the key.

Execution checked against lines 5-7. Own verbs (look, dash off) break the exact-word twin. Window overlap stays tied between the key and the pheasant option, so the overlap tell does not return.

Lines 13-14 run 'Mrs. Otis, at Lady Canterville's earnest request, had consented'. The option reverses asker and agreer, which is en-agent-patient-reversal, and it is wrong under every reading. Execution checked. 'Consented' and 'earnest' are the passage's own words and were already on the row. It is no longer the key's near-twin.

Lines 9-10 have Tom answer 'No' and then 'no, I sha'n't'. 'He says he will' drops the negative, which is en-negation-dropped. Execution checked: he says no twice. Naming Maggie and Tom pairs it with the reversal option ('Tom asks whether Maggie...'), so the closest pair now holds no key (measure after: twin pair = distractor). The key becomes the option with the fewest window words, a content tell running far under chance in retrieval (x0.10), which is not a giveaway.

Maggie's guess is the tipsy-cake (line 16). It is Tom who knows the pudding will be apricot roll-up (lines 18-19), so 'which is what Maggie has guessed' is false under every reading. Swapping who knows is en-agent-patient-reversal, the same mistake as the stored value with a different frame. Execution checked. The 'The pudding, which...' twin with the key is broken.

Round-1 faults fixed: no lifted 'power of sacrifice', and the value is cleanly false. Lines 33-35 say she 'cared less that Tom should enjoy the utmost possible amount of puff, than that he should be pleased with her'. 'Only cares' about his puff reverses that ranking, so no reading supports it. en-relation-word-flipped fits: the comparison 'less ... than' is misread and the two wants change places. 'Should enjoy' is the passage's construction and is grammatical British English, not contorted. Execution facts checked (lines 33-35). Ties the key at 12 words; passage overlap no longer picks the key.

Execution facts checked. 'Imaginary elephant hunt' fairly names 'Suppose I was shooting an elephant'. Ties 15 words and breaks the made-up-example twin.
